another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's start by finding out about your child. **How old is your child?**

This is important because eligibility rules differ based on age:
- **Under 16**: Generally eligible (subject to other conditions)
- **16 to 19**: May be eligible if in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me your child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son **Alex, who is 16 years old**.

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, his eligibility will depend on whether he's in approved education or training. Let me check the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training situation.

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In approved education or training** (at school, college, or on an approved training program), OR
2. **Has he recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks), OR
3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in education or training at the moment - he left school a while back and hasn't started anything new yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex left school a while back and isn't currently in education or training.

To determine his eligibility, I need to know more specifically: **When did Alex leave education or training?**

This is important because there's a possible extension period of up to 20 weeks after leaving approved education or training. If he left:
- **Within the last 20 weeks** - he might still be eligible during an extension period
- **More than 20 weeks ago** - he would not be eligible

Can you tell me approximately when he left school?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was more than 20 weeks ago - he's been out of school for quite a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me navigate to the appropriate outcome based on this situation.

conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Result: **INELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

### Why Alex doesn't qualify:

For young people aged 16-19, Child Benefit can only be claimed if they are in **approved education or training**. Since Alex:
- Is 16 years old
- Is not currently in education or training
- Left school more than 20 weeks ago (outside the extension period)

He does not meet the qualifying child criteria under the Child Benefit rules.

### What you could consider:

**If Alex returns to education or training:**
- If Alex enrolls in approved full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, T-levels, or similar qualifications at school or college), you would become eligible for Child Benefit again
- Approved training programs may also qualify

**Extension period:**
- When a 16-17 year old leaves education, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks if they register with a careers service or the armed services

**Other support:**
- You may want to explore other forms of financial support that might be available for your family situation

If Alex's circumstances change and he starts education or training, you can make a new claim at that time. If you have any questions or need further guidance, you can contact the Child Benefit Office directly.
